run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T21:51:15Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy's RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a burst of failed frontend requests between about 21:55Z and 22:05Z. frontend-proxy error spans on operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' (HTTP 500/503/504) rose from a 1.1-4.4 per 5m background to 121-497 per 5m at 21:55-22:05Z and were back to 1.1-4.3 from 22:06Z. frontend's own error spans are confined to GET /api/data -> executing api route /api/data -> grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, whose exact error text is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080', the ad Service ClusterIP. Deployment otel-demo/ad was rollout-restarted at 21:52:35Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, old ad-554b849958 scaled to 0); the new ad container started at 21:52:37Z but emitted its first line 'Ad service starting.' only at 21:57:24.907Z, produced zero spans during 21:55-22:00Z while sibling services served traffic without errors, refused connections, then served with 13-14s GetAds p95 against a 157-349ms baseline until about 22:05Z. Because the claim naming the Deployment restart as the origin is a hypothesis and the immediate reason the restarted container was not serving promptly is not directly measured, the conclusion is partial. Alternative candidates were checked and rejected: the flagd flag adFailure='on' does not match the observed TCP-level refusal, ad still returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and errors cleared while the flag remained 'on'; flagd was not globally slow because cart's flagd calls stayed healthy; node pressure was absent.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) sat at 1.1-4.4 per 5m through 21:54Z, jumped to 121.1 at 21:55Z, peaked at 496.7 at 21:59Z, stayed 47.8-488.9 through 22:05Z, and fell back to 1.1-4.3 from 22:06Z; the erroring operations are 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'.

In the 5m window ending 22:00Z, frontend-proxy had 488.9 error spans out of 6120 total span increase and frontend had 973.3 out of 13280; the only services with non-zero error spans at that instant were frontend and frontend-proxy (recommendation, fraud-detection, ad, payment and accounting were 0).

frontend-proxy returns HTTP 500 (about 2ms), HTTP 503 (39ms-1.0s) and HTTP 504 (15.0s, upstream status 0) on its error spans during the spike; the 15s 504s correspond to frontend /api/data spans lasting up to 24.6s, exceeding the proxy's 15s route timeout.

frontend's error spans are confined to 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and the client span 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds', with identical per-5m counts (e.g. 54.4 at 21:55Z, 243.3 at 21:59Z); other frontend routes such as /api/cart and /api/checkout show 0 error spans.

The exact diagnostic on frontend's failing 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' span is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' with rpc.grpc.status_code=14; 100.70.197.56:8080 is the ClusterIP and port of Service otel-demo/ad, whose selector is opentelemetry.io/name=ad.

frontend's GetAds p95 latency was 157-349ms from 21:32-21:54Z, dropped to 3.4-14ms at 21:59-22:01Z (fast connection refusals), then rose to 13.1s-14.2s at 22:02-22:05Z, and returned to 342-358ms at 22:06-22:10Z.

The ad service emitted no spans at all in the 5m window ending 22:00Z (ad total span increase 0) while every other otel-demo service served traffic, e.g. cart 4831.1, checkout 2497.8, product-catalog 3166.7 and frontend 13280 span increase.

Deployment otel-demo/ad was restarted at 21:52:35Z: its pod template carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T21:52:35Z, the new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 was created 21:52:35Z and the old ad-554b849958 was scaled 1->0 at 21:52:37Z, with the Deployment events 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0', ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete, Deployment generation 2 and lastUpdateTime 21:52:37Z.

The rollout changed only the restartedAt annotation: both ad ReplicaSets use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad with identical resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi), so this was a restart with unchanged image and unchanged resource settings.

Pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh started its ad container at 21:52:37Z with restartCount 0, but its only log line before 21:57:30Z is 'Ad service starting.' at 21:57:24.907Z, about 4m47s after container start; the ad container defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe.

The ad pod became functional again from about 22:02Z: its logs show normal 'Targeted ad request received for [...]' lines from 22:02:18Z, and ad's own GetAds server-span p95 went 940ms (22:03Z), 783ms (22:04Z), 739ms (22:05Z) and 541ms (22:06Z) against a 21:32-21:54Z baseline of 84-195ms.

A full trace at 21:59:56Z shows the ad service could not keep up: ad's 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' span lasted 22.37s and returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, while its child 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' calls lasted 1.6s, 3.6s and 2.3s with rpc.grpc.status_code=4, and the flagd server span for one of them was only 9us with otel.status_description 'context deadline exceeded', the request reaching flagd about 2.6s after ad's client span started.

flagd was not globally slow during the incident: cart's 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' client spans ran at 126.7-183.3 per 5m with only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no error status) and p95 latency of 51-99ms throughout 21:55-22:05Z, the same period in which ad's flagd calls were timing out.

There is no node-level resource fault: all 5 nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, and the otel-demo services co-located with ad on node i-040b429451d033123 (frontend, frontend-proxy, cart, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, product-catalog, payment, currency, email, shipping, accounting, postgresql, valkey-cart, image-provider, quote) recorded 0 error spans at 22:00Z.

Service otel-demo/ad is a ClusterIP service on 100.70.197.56 with port and targetPort 8080 selecting opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and its Endpoints currently list a single address, pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh on port 8080, so a port mismatch between the Service and the container's declared containerPort 8080 is not visible in the current objects.

Background not tied to this deviation: fraud-detection's container last terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at 21:27:13Z (restartCount 1), about 25 minutes before the ad error surge, and fraud-detection shows 0 error spans at 22:00Z; the ad pod shows 0 restarts.

The origin is Deployment otel-demo/ad: its rollout restart at 21:52:35Z replaced the serving ad pod with pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, which did not accept connections on 8080 for roughly five minutes (first log at 21:57:24.907Z, zero ad spans 21:55-22:00Z) and then answered GetAds only after 13-24s, so frontend's /api/data calls to the ad Service failed first with ECONNREFUSED and then by timeout, producing frontend's 500s and frontend-proxy's 500/503/504 error rate, which returned to background once ad was serving again from about 22:02-22:06Z.

The reason the restarted ad container could not serve promptly is most likely CPU starvation of the ad container, whose limit is only 50m (10m request): it needed about 4m47s to reach its 'Ad service starting.' log, GetAds spent about 13.5s before its first traced child, ad's flagd requests reached flagd about 2.6s late while flagd itself answered in 9us, and flagd served cart normally at the same time. No container CPU throttling metric was available to confirm this.

The fault-injection flag adFailure (defaultVariant 'on', description 'Fail ad service') in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is not the cause of this error rate: the observed failure is a TCP-level 'connect ECONNREFUSED' to the ad ClusterIP and later 13-24s ad latencies, not an application-level ad failure; ad returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0 for GetAds at 22:00:27Z inside the failure window; and frontend-proxy's error rate had already returned to its 1-4 per 5m background by 22:06Z while the flag still read 'on' at 22:16Z.

A flagd-wide outage or latency regression is not supported: cart's flagd ResolveBoolean calls continued at about 126-183 per 5m with no error status and p95 51-99ms across the whole spike window, and flagd's own server span in the ad trace processed the late request in 9us.

Node-level CPU or memory pressure and a request flood are not supported: every node is Ready with no pressure conditions, all co-located otel-demo services on ad's node had 0 error spans at 22:00Z, and frontend-proxy's total span volume (6120 per 5m at 22:00Z) is in line with the pre-incident ingress-plus-egress volume of roughly 2900-3400 per 5m, so there is no evidence of a traffic spike.

Review the ad workload's restart safety: add a readiness probe and a startupProbe on the ad container's port 8080 so a starting ad pod is not kept in the ad Service endpoints, and raise the ad container CPU limit above 50m so a restart does not need minutes of throttled startup.

Confirm who or what applied the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T21:52:35Z patch to Deployment ad, and whether it was intended to reload the flagd flags; change history is not integrated in this Run, so this cannot be established from the available evidence.

Re-check the RequestErrorRate alert rule: its expression is not loaded in this Prometheus, so the annotation value 2.4555555555555553 could not be reconciled, and frontend-proxy carried a non-zero background error rate of 1.1-4.4 error spans per 5m before the deviation, which matters for an 'above 0' style threshold.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not available: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate (d596beb2-1241-4bea-8b63-0c2bb0c21f55-t0:5eace6aa-cce9-401c-bb3c-929d115ad1b4) and with no filter (562bfb04-f4f4-486d-91b6-a1320d6038aa-t2:8e8a4ca0-9e96-44fb-bcc4-3dc96dda7e9d) both returned no data, so the rule expression and threshold, and why activeAt is 21:51:15Z (before the first observed error-rate jump at 21:55Z), are unknown; the annotation's 'current: 2.4555555555555553' could not be reproduced from any available series.

No container CPU throttling metrics (e.g. container_cpu_cfs_throttled_*) exist in this Prometheus, so the hypothesis that the 50m CPU limit throttled the ad container's startup and request handling is unverified.

kube_pod_status_* and kube_deployment_status_* series returned no data (64858a36-f80a-401d-ac7b-c328e5d4fbb8-t0:8f100870-378e-47ba-9c55-514f10879336, 64858a36-f80a-401d-ac7b-c328e5d4fbb8-t2:15d0437e-fa16-4968-a425-1d7050056844, ca87a9dd-a78b-4a40-bf88-79dc58385a43-t2:9b96359b-e996-4ee6-a68e-abd5694dbcb8), so the ad pod's Ready and endpoint timeline during the incident cannot be observed directly.

The NetworkPolicy query returned no data (a3af4be1-2c0f-4f9c-90bb-0a0d6eed014f-t2:661193c7-da7a-4a85-90f7-18dc7cad2812), so whether any NetworkPolicy governed traffic to ad during the window is unknown rather than zero.

No HTTP-level proxy metrics exist here (8231d729-ed85-4d99-8463-b125534451fb-t0:19881fa4-cd6e-41c3-b80e-8838ae506f56 returned nothing for http_*|envoy_*|nginx_*), so the alert's error-rate reading could belong to a source outside this Prometheus.

frontend container logs are empty/unavailable for 21:50-22:10Z (dda231ce-2457-4cdd-ae19-5ef7556de50a-t0:87f208a6-55a9-412e-b4f8-d8f8c2f127dd and 86523f5f-3746-4a46-8f86-c4fc3e48ba06-t0:bbd0bf5e-f662-418a-844f-39ffe084470d returned 0 lines), so the frontend's own error log lines could not be read.

flagd produced no log lines in 21:50-22:10Z (c46e529a-2950-44f5-b2f9-22e597f0f93b-t2:8782b48d-4f4a-4560-88a2-cc7032250111) and has no traces_span_metrics series (c46e529a-2950-44f5-b2f9-22e597f0f93b-t0:45a064cd-9a2a-4d52-846e-825492df4c5b and c46e529a-2950-44f5-b2f9-22e597f0f93b-t1:6b87a172-55b5-4f10-ab7a-cefb3bb2586c returned no data), so flagd's own view of the incident is unknown apart from the single server span inside the sampled trace.
The old ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was deleted and its logs are not retrievable, and the new ad container has no previous instance, so pre-restart ad behavior cannot be compared directly.

The change_history integration is not available and ConfigMaps cannot prove past values: when adFailure and the other flagd flags were set, and whether the flagd configuration changed at about 21:52Z, could not be verified.

Queries for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count (49c6bf97-4c6f-4ade-a726-548d0c241bce-t0:ed128aad-ece8-4347-a764-d88be3326bd2), for the frontend GetAds error tag (49c6bf97-4c6f-4ade-a726-548d0c241bce-t1:8c216b25-ddc1-4e17-a2b5-d0267a562141) and for service_name on that metric (5c607791-7d8f-42a2-8033-2df2276ae81e-t1:bbdf512a-39e1-4b9f-b0ba-49c7eb95440b) returned no data, so gRPC status-code labels from runtime metrics are unavailable and the gRPC view rests on trace spans.
Traces and span metrics are sampled views, so error and span counts are lower bounds; the ad service's zero span count in 21:55-22:00Z means no spans were recorded, not that no packets arrived.
next_steps: Retrieve the Alertmanager rule or dashboard expression for RequestErrorRate in the monitoring stack that owns it, and confirm the 21:51:15Z activeAt against frontend-proxy's background error rate.
Check the audit log or CI/CD change record for the Deployment otel-demo/ad patch at 2026-11-16T21:52:35Z and for flagd-config edits around the same time.

Review container CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total / throttled_seconds_total) for pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh from a runtime metrics source that carries it, and compare JVM startup time against the previous ad pod.
If adFailure is not intended to be enabled, reset the flagd flag adFailure to 'off'; it is a declared fault-injection setting even though it did not match this failure path.
Consider a synthetic canary of Service otel-demo/ad port 8080 after any ad Deployment restart to catch a pod that is in Endpoints before its process is listening.
